detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Surrey, 1894, afternoon sun from the left, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:07. The shot opens on an insert on the thin bright seam at the edge of the crusted lid: the steel tip of a workman's pickaxe already scraping along the smooth curve of the lid, sliding off the crust; only that object and what touches it is in frame. The camera is at the foot of the lid, an arm's length from the seam, a 90mm lens. The afternoon sun comes from the LEFT along the seam. At the first frame the thin bright seam curves across the CENTRE of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge. The dun-grey crust of the lid fills the TOP half, the steel pickaxe tip scrapes at the RIGHT third, and the crust of the body fills the BOTTOM third below the seam. The shot is inside this place: The same great raw crater on Horsell Common on a glaring hot summer afternoon in 1894: the sand walls dug back and scored by spades, planks and pickaxes on the gravel floor, the colossal crusted cylinder thirty yards across lying half-buried, much more of its long hull now uncovered. The camera tracks sideways to the left along the seam, past the scraping pickaxe tip as the pickaxe slides off the smooth crust and skids along the seam, from 00:00 to 00:04. At 00:04 grey clinker dust drifts down the curve, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:07 the camera is tracking through the last frame, and the action continues with it.

overall_soundscape: The ambience of the same great raw crater on Horsell Common on a glaring hot summer afternoon in 1894: the sand walls dug back and scored by spades runs under the whole take: its own air, the surfaces underfoot and the fabric of the place around it. Cloth, boots and the small sounds of hands on wood, glass and iron carry the physical action throughout.
